title: How Zach Yadegari scaled Cal AI to $30M revenue and sold it to MyFitnessPal at 19
summary: Zach explains how Cal AI grew from influencer marketing to performance ads and how he ran his first acquisition. He covers playing hard to get, warm intros, expected-value thinking, and how he validates app ideas by treating competitors as proof of demand.

principles.text: Influencer marketing got Cal AI to ~$2M/month; performance ads on Instagram, TikTok and Facebook unlocked the next stage.
principles.quote: influencer marketing is what started us and it took us really far. We got to about $2 million a month just from influencer marketing. The thing is after that we kind of plateaued a little bit.

principles.text: A big creator sponsorship can pay back through credibility that unlocks more deals, even if the direct return is unprofitable.
principles.quote: having the brand name Mr. be saying we were in a video, we were able to do way more deals afterwards. We had way more credibility with our brand

principles.text: When selling a company, get warm intros rather than cold outreach, since cold outreach loses leverage.
principles.quote: I was recommended that or I heard somewhere it's you lose leverage if you're just cold outreaching.

principles.text: In acquisition talks, play hard to get: show interest but signal you're going somewhere regardless.
principles.quote: you basically want to play hard to get kind of you don't want to you don't want to be too interested.

principles.text: Use expected value to weigh selling now versus keep going, instead of deciding on emotion.
principles.quote: EV is a good one. So, like gamblers obviously know this where it's like the percent chance of winning something and then the prize and you multiply them together.

principles.text: Skill at validating ideas matters more than generating them; an existing competitor is proof of demand, not a reason to quit.
principles.quote: I think the more important skill and the better skill is a framework to validate what is a good idea because you could come up with ideas all the time
